name: NiMH and NiCd cells
summary: Rechargeable nickel cells: AA and AAA NiMH, and older NiCd packs in drills, phones and toys.
uses: Solar garden lights and small solar kits
Rebuilding old drill and tool packs
identify: AA, AAA, C, D or sub-C cells marked NiMH or Ni-Cd and 1.2V. Packs of sub-C cells hide in older cordless drills, cordless phones, emergency lights, RC toys and solar garden lights. NiCd holds toxic cadmium: don’t burn or crush it.
test: A charged cell reads 1.3–1.4V and a flat one about 1.0–1.2V. Cells left flat for months often come back after two or three full charge cycles.

decay.note: They self-discharge within months but usually recover with a few full charges; NiCd packs last longer.
